name: St. Johns

boundaries.north: Columbia Slough / Smith and Bybee Wetlands

characteristics.housing_stock: 1910s-1930s Craftsman bungalows and foursquares, some Victorians, postwar ranches on perimeter
characteristics.transit_access: Moderate — frequent bus on Lombard, Yellow Line MAX at Expo Center (edge of neighborhood), St. Johns Bridge connects to NW but limited cross-town options
characteristics.development_pipeline: Cathedral Park neighborhood improvements, St. Johns town center streetscape work, some mixed-use infill on Lombard

investment_thesis: Island neighborhood with strong identity and character. Cathedral Park and St. Johns Bridge provide genuine charm that drives buyer interest. Craftsman housing stock is ideal for high-return renovations — older homes with period details command premium after thoughtful rehab. Relative geographic isolation creates a micro-market with loyal buyers. Town center has good walkable retail. Best for investors who can source off-market deals through local relationships.
risk_factors: Geographic isolation from rest of Portland — bridges and distance limit commute options
Flood zone concerns in lower areas near Columbia Slough
Industrial neighbors (Port of Portland, rail yards) impact some blocks
Limited transit — car-dependent for many destinations
Some legacy environmental contamination near industrial corridor
data_sources: Synthetic MLS data based on market knowledge
